memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the days of mourning had passed, Joseph said to Pharaoh's court, 'If I have found favour in your eyes, speak to Pharaoh for me. Tell him, "My father made me swear an oath and said, 'I am about to die; bury me in the tomb I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.' Now let me go up and bury my father; then I will return."' Pharaoh said, 'Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.'" — Gen 50:4-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph is second only to Pharaoh. He could almost certainly have gone without asking. Instead he requests permission, respectfully, through proper channels — "If I have found favour in your eyes."

There is real character in that. Power does not exempt a person from courtesy. Joseph has authority, and he still submits it to the one above him rather than acting as though he answers to nobody.

Notice too what he is asking for. Permission to keep a promise. Jacob made him swear an oath, and Joseph intends to honour it exactly, even though the man he promised is now dead and would never know if he did not.

That is the test of integrity. Keeping your word when the other person cannot check. Psalm 15 describes the person who may dwell with God as one who keeps an oath even when it hurts (Ps 15:4).

And Jesus said something similar in far simpler terms: let your yes be yes and your no be no (Matt 5:37). Christians should be people whose word does not need enforcing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you keep promises even when nobody would know if you did not?
2. Does having authority make you more or less courteous?
3. Is there a commitment you have quietly let slide?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, make me a person of my word, whether or not anyone is checking. Give me humility with whatever authority You have entrusted to me. Amen.
